newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-US housing starts remain on solid ground.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-US housing starts remain on solid ground.

text.p: Financial markets can expect little change in U.S. housing starts for May, suggesting the housing sector is still supported by a solid economic foundation, analysts said.
Preliminary results of a Reuters poll showed economists project an average annual rate of 1.47 million starts in May, virtually unchanged from the reading in April.
But analysts said the robust growth in new homes and apartments over the first quarter is likely to scale back to more-sustainable levels in the forseeable future.
"What we have in place will be a very gently slowing trend over the balance of the year," said Joseph Liro, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp.
The May report is scheduled for release by the Commerce Department at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT on Tuesday.
Liro projected a headline starts number of 1.43 million, which would be down about 2.7 percent from April.
Lumber prices have fallen modestly between April and May, suggesting that demand for wood is beginning to slow a bit, he said.
Housing numbers probably peaked in the first quarter, said Liro. But as long as single-family homes continue to be erected at a 700,000 pace, "home builders are happy," he said.
"That is a very healthy level. You are not going to get growth, but you are going to sustain what are very satisfactory levels in this sector," Liro added.

Russell Sheldon, vice president and senior economist at Mellon Bank Corp, said the single-family sector should continue to show strength, feeding the economy in terms of furniture sales and other housing-related consumer spending.

But he expected a decline in multi-family housing starts, which rose to 355,000 in April from a revised 320,000 in March. "(April) was extraordinarily strong and there is no real reason to think that the industry is growing at that pace," Sheldon said.
Some analysts forecast overall housing starts edged up slightly, bolstered by stable mortgage rates and low supply.

"You've had a new situation in which mortgage interest rates broadly speaking have been fairly stable, and we have a situation where the supply of housing to be sold is relatively low," said John Ryding, senior economist at Bear Stearns & Co.
"So those forces tend to keep people filing permits," said Ryding, who forecast starts to creep up to 1.49 million units.

Ryding said that the level of permits last month -- 1.44 million -- along with the shift in the weather and a modest increase in hours worked in the construction industry, may have increased housing starts modestly.
